set.st: Lee Horning, an eccentric money-lender who never used a bank and was said to have 'some secret hiding place', lived alone in a little house in the north part of Algona. He died on 23 May 1893 without a will, the day after arranging a $600 loan. His garden was spaded over and the house and outbuildings searched; only $1 was found, and the leading rumour was that someone had already taken the money. Kossuth papers mention him to 1899 without any find. In April 1899 'the Lee Horning house on the new school house site' was sold at auction for $20 and ground was broken for the new school, a $17,600 building by the Gross Construction Co., so his lot became the site of Algona's new 1899 school. Pin is the town, not the lot.

src: Algona Republican, 12 Apr 1899, p. 5 (the Lee Horning house sold at auction for $20; ground broken for the new school building; Newspapers.com 2309525)
